summary: Yasumasa Sekine is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS. He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Gakushuin Women's Junior College, University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

Yasunori Ejima (1939–1999) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his degrees, including a doctorate, from the University of Tokyo, where he later served as associate professor (1982) and professor (1987, 1995–1999). He taught Kei Kataoka.

Yasuo Deguchi is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral course at Kyoto University (~1989–1994). He taught at Nagoya Institute of Technology before returning to Kyoto University, where he became professor in 2016 and dean in 2023.

Yasuo Goto is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held teaching posts at Ryukoku University (attested in 1991 as lecturer and in 2006 as part-time lecturer) and served as a part-time lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2006).

Yasuo Inamoto specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a technical official at Nara National Museum (~1996–2004) and held a post at Kyoto University starting around 2004.

Yasuo Matsunami (1948–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano, later serving there as a lecturer (attested 1992–2006) and as an advisor to the Śrāvakabhūmi Study Group until 2010.
Yasuo Sano is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

Yasuo Yuasa (1925–2005) worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji, later holding professorships at Osaka University (1975) and the University of Tsukuba (1981–1989), and taught Gereon Kopf.

Yasuro Abe works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Wako and Otani universities. His appointments include assistant at Osaka University, associate professor at Otemae University, professor at Nagoya University (1998), and professor at Ryukoku University (2019).

Yasusaburo Sakaki (1870–1929) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1890–1895) and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1897–1903) and Kyushu University (~1906–1928). He taught Gikyo Ito.

Yasushi Endo is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held positions at Nagoya University, served as a professor at Shitennoji University (attested 2000), and was a full-time lecturer at Aichi Bunkyo University (attested 2000–2004).

Yasutaka Muroya is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He has served as a project research associate at the University of Vienna and the University of Leipzig, and as a research associate at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Yasutoshi Murakami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1960–1970). He held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1972–1987) and Koyasan University (~1987), and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).
Yawen Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed an MA degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).

Yelena Rudenko is an Indology and history scholar. She studied at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, University of Delhi, and R. B. Suleimenov Institute of Oriental Studies, later working as a research fellow there (2006–2019) and lecturing at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University.
Yellava Subbarayalu is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a professor at Tamil University and as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (attested 2015).

Yeshe Thupten is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held appointments as a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia (1982) and at Middlebury College (1982), and taught Daniel Cozort, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and Joe Bransford Wilson.

Yeshi Donden (1927–2019) studied at Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine under Khyenrab Norbu. In 1961 he founded the Men-Tsee-Khang, serving as its director until 1966. He taught Marsha Woolf, Elisabeth Finckh, and Eliot Tokar.
Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner (attested 2001) and taught Huidi Zeng.

Yifa works in Buddhist studies. She studied at National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. She served as department head and dean at the University of the West (~1996–2004) and founded the Woodenfish Foundation.
